newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Eight Taiwan firms awarded mobile data licences.
newsitem.headline: Eight Taiwan firms awarded mobile data licences.

text.p: Taiwan has awarded mobile data licences to eight local firms, but withheld nine franchises due to the ineligibility of the bidders, a senior official said on Tuesday.
"We were scheduled to issue 17 licences, but of the 31 bidders, we only found eight were qualified," Su Tsung-hung, a telecom official at the transport ministry, told Reuters.

All eight winning bidders are backed by major Taiwan firms, including ChinaTrust Commercial Bank, Eternal Chemical, GVC Corp, Microelectronics Technology Inc., Synnex Technology International and Tai-I.
Mobile data is a service that allows transfer of data to users over radio frequencies. The bidders envisage selling stock market prices and other valuable information over such systems.

The dismantling of Taiwan's telecom monopoly is a key liberalisation aimed at ensuring the island's entry to the World Trade Organisation and establish it as an attractive Asia-Pacific operations hub for transnational firms.
Other sectors being liberalised include mobile telephony, paging systems and trunking radio.
Analysts expect the local telecom market, long monopolised by the state, to double in size in three to five years as new entrants are allowed to compete with state-run Chunghwa Telecom.

"With the technical back-up of their foreign partners, these new telecom ventures should boost the local market's turnover to double in three to five years after they begin operations," said Alex Chen, assistant rerearch head of HSBC James Capel Taiwan.
"The new ventures are expected to start having profits three to five years after starting operations," Chen said.
